newsitem.title: USA: Wendy's could have 10,000 stores by 2001-CEO.
newsitem.headline: Wendy's could have 10,000 stores by 2001-CEO.

text.p: Wendy's International Inc could have 10,000 Wendy's and Tim Hortons restaurants by 2000-2001, chairman, president and chief executive officer Gorton Teter told Reuters Thursday.
"We believe it's realistic that, between Wendy's and Tim Hortons -- which now have 6,500 stores -- certainly by 2000-2001, we could have 10,000 stores worldwide," he said.
He spoke after an opening ceremony for a combination Wendy's-Tim Hortons unit in this Columbus, Ohio, suburb.
Wendy's acquired Canada-based Hortons in 1995. Hortons coffee/pastry units do most of their business in the morning. Wendy's sells hamburgers and other lunch/evening fare.
The store opening marked the 5,000th Wendy's unit in the world, the 1,500th Tim Hortons and the third U.S. combination unit. Other combined units are in Detroit and Minneapolis.
Teter said plans call for three more such combination units in Detroit, three more in Columbus and some in Boston.
Wendy's plans about 30 stand-alone and combination Tim Hortons in Columbus by yearend, including conversion of some stores acquired from another chain last year, he said.
Wendy's television spokesman and founder Dave Thomas, looking healthy after heart bypass surgery in December, was also a speaker at the restaurant opening.
Thomas will continue to star in new advertising for Wendy's, executive vice president Charles Rath said.

As reported, Teter said he does not believe a promotion expected soon from competitor McDonald's Corp will have an impact on Wendy's sales and earnings. McDonald's is expected to launch a 55-cent sandwich promotion in April.
